date: The Khaybar Expedition, 7th year of the Hijra (628)
title: 162nk1o
Khaybar and the Banner: "I Will Give It to One Who Loves God and His Messenger"
hook: Khaybar held out for days. The Prophet gave the banner to Imam Ali, whom God and His Messenger love.
scenes.0.text: In the 7th year of the Hijra, the Prophet marched to **Khaybar**, north of Medina. The fortresses stood side by side. The army besieged them one by one. This expedition was to show that **Imam Ali** protected the Prophet's cause.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.1.text: At Khaybar, one of the fortresses could not be taken for days. It is related that first Abu Bakr, then Umar went with the banner. Both returned without completing the conquest. The fortress was still standing. The banner had not yet been given to the one who would take the fortress.
scenes.2.text: Thereupon the Prophet said: "Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves God and His Messenger, and whom God and His Messenger love. God will bring the conquest through his hand." That night the soldiers in the tents stayed up until morning, talking about to whom the banner would be given.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.text: In the morning, everyone before Khaybar hoped for the banner. The Prophet asked, "Where is Ali?" **Imam Ali**'s eyes were aching. They brought him. The Prophet applied his saliva to his eyes. The eyes opened. He gave the banner to **Imam Ali**. Imam Ali asked: "O Messenger of God, shall I fight them until they become Muslims like us?" The Prophet said to him: "Go gently. When you reach their land, first invite them to Islam. Inform them of the rights of God that are upon them. I swear by God that **for God to guide a single person through you is better for you than owning red camels**."
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.4.text: Before the gate of Khaybar, the Jewish warrior **Marhab** came out into the field. His helmet was on his head, his armor on his body. Brandishing his sword, he recited a rajaz: "Khaybar knows that I am Marhab. My weapons are complete, I am a hero seasoned in battle. When war flares, I am there." **Imam Ali** stood before him and answered with rajaz: "I am the one whom my mother named Haydar. Haydar means lion. I am fierce of look like a lion of the forest." According to the narration, Imam Ali brought down Dhu al-Fiqar **without receiving a single wound**. A single blow split Marhab's helmet and head in two from the top. **Marhab fell to the ground and died.** The Jewish warriors were stricken with terror. The fortress was conquered after this blow.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.5.text: According to the narration, **Imam Ali** tore the gate of Khaybar from its place and used it as a shield. He held the gate before him while fighting.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.6.text: The banner had been given to the one who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by God and His Messenger. That person was **Imam Ali**. It is also related that the Prophet said, "He is not one who flees, he is one who attacks." Beside those who had returned the day before without completing the conquest, this saying clearly showed the place of **Imam Ali**.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.text: When Khaybar was conquered, the people remained in place, to give half of the produce. The people of **Fadak** came to terms without fighting. The land came into the Prophet's hands. He gave this land as a hiba to his daughter **Lady Fatima**. Hiba means gift. But this gift would be taken from **Lady Fatima**'s hand after the Messenger of God's death, and Fadak **would be usurped**.
sunni.0.says: At Khaybar the banner is given to the one who loves God and His Messenger. Imam Ali's eyes are opened. Imam Ali says, "Shall I fight them until they become like us?" The Prophet tells him to go gently, to invite them to Islam, and states that guiding one person is better than red camels.
sunni.1.says: The banner is given to Imam Ali. Imam Ali asks, "Shall I fight them until they become Muslims like us?" The Prophet: go gently, when you reach their land, invite them to Islam, inform them of the rights of God. "For God to guide one person through you is better than red camels." The text was read at No. 3009; the Maghazi number is cited as 4210.
sunni.2.says: The same banner dialogue. Imam Ali says, "O Messenger of God, shall I fight them until they become like us?" The Prophet tells him to proceed gently, invite them to Islam, and inform them of the rights of God. Guiding one person is better than owning red camels.
sunni.3.says: It is related that after the two earlier attempts, the banner was given to Imam Ali.
sunni.4.says: Marhab comes out into the field in armor saying "Khaybar knows that I am Marhab." Imam Ali replies, "I am the one whom my mother named Haydar," strikes him on the head and kills him. The conquest takes place through his hand. Splitting the helmet from the top in two, receiving no wound, and going to Hell are not in this text.
shia.0.says: The giving of the banner to Imam Ali at Khaybar, the narration of the gate, and the account of the event in Shia sources.
shia.1.says: Imam Ali's killing of Marhab at Khaybar. The splitting of the helmet and head in two with a single blow was not tied to a separate page. It was set apart in the scene as an Ahl al-Bayt narration. A page number was not given separately.
shia.2.says: Marhab's rajaz, Imam Ali's Haydar rajaz, and the killing of Marhab. A page number was not given separately.
disputes.0.title: 1smrgrr
What does the banner saying show?
disputes.0.shia: The Prophet said he would give the Khaybar banner to the one who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by them; that person was Imam Ali. In Shia thought, the saying's being specific to him shows his place and merit before the Prophet; the failure of the two earlier attempts makes this difference clear.
disputes.0.sunni: The Prophet said he would give the Khaybar banner to the one who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by them; that person was Imam Ali. In the Sunni reading, this is a great merit; there are similar praises for other Companions as well, and the saying is not counted as proof of the caliphate.
disputes.1.title: 7duodm
The narration of Abu Bakr and Umar
disputes.1.shia: A narration that the banner was given first to Abu Bakr and then to Umar is mentioned in al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak and Ahmad b. Hanbal, Musnad. The Shia cite this narration as important evidence alongside the subsequent giving of the banner to Imam Ali.
disputes.1.sunni: A narration that the banner was given first to Abu Bakr and then to Umar is mentioned in al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak and Ahmad b. Hanbal, Musnad. In the Sunni reading, the authenticity of this narration is disputed; this detail is not in the narrations of Bukhari and Muslim.
disputes.2.title: 7tadab
The narration of the gate
disputes.2.shia: It is related that Imam Ali tore the gate of Khaybar from its place and used it. In Shia thought, this is an indication of his extraordinary strength.
disputes.2.sunni: It is related that Imam Ali tore the gate of Khaybar from its place and used it. Sunni hadith scholars regard the chain of this narration as weak; it is not found in the sahih sources.
questions.0: The Prophet gave the banner to Imam Ali, who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by them. How does this saying nourish your love for him?
questions.1: Bukhari and Muslim relate that the banner was given to Imam Ali. What awakens within you as you read this shared scene?
questions.2: The saying "who loves God and His Messenger" was said for Imam Ali. How does this love describe to you his place beside the Prophet?
summary: At Khaybar, the Prophet said he would give the banner to the one who loves God and His Messenger and is loved by them. That person was Imam Ali. This saying also appears in Sunni sources (Bukhari, Sahih, no. 2942; Muslim, Sahih, no. 2406). The Shia take it as evidence of Imam Ali's place beside the Prophet.
key: The banner was given to Imam Ali, who loves God and His Messenger
notes.0: Khaybar was a Jewish oasis north of Medina in the 7th year of the Hijra.
notes.1: One of the fortresses could not be taken for days.
notes.2: The Prophet said, «I will give the banner to one who loves God and His Messenger» (Bukhari 2942, Muslim 2406).
notes.3: The banner was given to Imam Ali; his eyes were healed by the Prophet's saliva.
notes.4: This saying is a sign of Imam Ali's being chosen.
